title: The manhood of Christ as beginning of the fairest ways of righteousness
english: For the manhood of Christ has become for us the beginning of the fairest ways of righteousness, leading us to better pursuits.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Eustathius is opening his argument that Christ's manhood is the starting point of the fairest paths of righteousness, leading believers to better pursuits.

title: Christ's manhood joins, guides, and restores; then Christ's own saying
english: Christ's manhood joins us fittingly to the Spirit, guides us into paradise, and restores us to our proper pasture. Therefore Christ also said, “I am the way and the truth and the life” (John 14:6).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Eustathius is describing what the manhood of Christ does for believers, then introduces Christ's saying from John 14:6.

title: The names way, truth, and life signify two natures
english: By the name “way,” then, he indicates the covering that belongs to his manhood—the covering that is one of the bodily and visible things. For a way is a portion of earth and stands as a perceptible ground. But the name “truth” and “life” indicates the nature of the Father, since truth is an intelligible thing that falls under neither eyes nor touch.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Eustathius is explaining the meaning of Christ's saying 'I am the way and the truth and the life' from John 14:6, distinguishing what each name signifies.
